questions.question: Unless a package is clearly unsafe, what does a driver need to accept it?
questions.explanation: Shippers certify that hazardous materials are packaged correctly. You can accept a package if the shipper certifies it is safe and follows Hazardous Materials Regulations, unless the package looks clearly unsafe.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, what should you do with the liquid discharge valves?
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves closed on a compressed gas tank except when loading or unloading.

questions.question: Some areas have restrictions on transporting explosives or hazardous waste. What should you do about these restrictions?

options.text: They are usually not a concern
Research them before choosing your route
They only apply if transporting more than 1,000 pounds

questions.correctAnswerText: Research them before choosing your route
questions.explanation: Before transporting hazardous materials, check what restrictions apply to the routes you plan to take.

questions.question: Which agency conducts the background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: When applying for a HazMat endorsement, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts a federal security check.

questions.question: How should placards be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: In any way, as long as they are visible
So words and numbers can be read from left to right
Within three inches of other markings

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers can be read from left to right
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed so any words or numbers read from left to right. Keep them at least three inches away from other markings.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, what should you do with the engine?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids, unless you need to run the engine to operate a pump. Ground the tank before opening it and keep it grounded until closing.

questions.question: If a box contains liquid containers, what marking must it display?

options.text: Arrows showing the correct upright direction

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing the correct upright direction
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must have orientation arrows showing which direction should be upright.

questions.question: If a hazardous materials item is too small for a label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: Tie it with other hazardous materials and place a paper label on the outside of the bundle
Attach the label to a tag securely fastened to the package
Mark it with a large orange dot
Place it in a box with a warning label

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag securely fastened to the package
questions.explanation: If a label is too large for the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: What indicates that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums are commonly used to hold and transport hazardous materials. The type of container can indicate if materials are hazardous.

questions.question: How should hazardous materials be loaded and unloaded?
questions.explanation: Heat makes many hazardous materials more dangerous. Always load and unload hazardous materials away from heat sources.

questions.question: Are shipping papers required?

options.text: Yes, for all shipments of hazardous materials.
Only if stored in a special cab compartment.
Only if kept as a digital file.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, for all shipments of hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous materials shipments. They tell drivers and workers about the cargo risks.

questions.question: When can Class 3 flammable liquids be moved from one tank to another?

options.text: On the roadway as long as no other people are nearby.
Only off public roads, unless there is an emergency.
At night when hidden from view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only off public roads, unless there is an emergency.
questions.explanation: Do not transfer flammable liquids from one vehicle to another on public roads unless there is an emergency. Always warn others about the hazards.

questions.question: What should you do if cargo is leaking?

options.text: Touch it to identify what it is.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify it.
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks, identify it using shipping papers or labels. Do not touch leaking material.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guidebook lists all hazardous chemicals and their identification numbers.

questions.question: Where must a person attending a placarded vehicle be located?

options.text: Inside a gas station looking through a window.
In the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake in the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: Which is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers. Directions are not.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when loading corrosive materials?
questions.explanation: Keep corrosive containers in their correct upright position. Do not drop or roll them.

questions.question: How should placards be used when transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: They should be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
They should be used only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When required, hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What must a person supervising tank loading do?

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A supervisor must be alert, have a clear view, stay within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards, know what to do in emergencies, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials. The shipper must also provide placards.

questions.question: Unless a package is clearly unsafe, what does the driver need to accept hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: If a package is not clearly unsafe and follows the rules, you can accept the shipper's certification that it was packaged correctly.

questions.question: What should a carrier do if hazardous materials are not properly prepared?

options.text: Accept the shipment, but make a note on the paperwork

questions.explanation: A carrier must refuse any shipment of hazardous materials that is not properly prepared.

questions.question: What does RQ stand for?
questions.explanation: RQ stands for reportable quantity. On shipping papers, RQ can be used instead of an X in the HM column to mark materials that must be identified.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should not be:

options.text: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge
Parked within 40 feet of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge
questions.explanation: Do not park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Only brief parking is allowed for vehicle operation needs like refueling. Never park within 5 feet of the road.

questions.question: If you apply for a HazMat endorsement, which agency must check your background?
questions.explanation: To get a new or renewed hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a background check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Do not use cargo heaters when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: If there is a collision with a vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives, the driver should:

options.text: Not warn others of the danger
Keep the explosives in the vehicle until after separating from the other vehicle
Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating from the other vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating from the other vehicle
questions.explanation: If you are in a collision with a vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives, warn others, keep people away, and do not allow smoking or open fires. Remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any occupied buildings before separating the vehicles.

questions.question: To operate a vehicle that transports hazardous materials, a driver must have:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a passenger endorsement
A CDL with an air brake endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a commercial driver license with a hazardous materials endorsement before driving any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials, even if it is not carrying hazardous materials at the time.

questions.question: What is used to warn people about hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped warning signs called placards are placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials to warn people.
